stop_condition: every acceptance criterion in the SPEC is traced to a test; the REVIEW-ARTIFACT-RECONCILED non-governing guarantee holds by construction against a crafted reason; and following the review_artifact_unrecorded refusal advice VERBATIM leaves gate resolvable and approve able to succeed on BOTH backlog shapes

findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:4996-5003 (unrecorded_current_advice and the review_artifact_unrecorded refusal it is interpolated into); the missing control is .claude/scripts/tests/review-separation.test.sh section 8.3
findings.evidence: R13-F1's fix is the RECONCILED grammar, and that mechanism is correct. The refusal MESSAGE it ships is not: unrecorded_max_iter (qa-gate.sh:4974) is the highest iteration among the UNRECORDED files only, and the message then asserts that file 'is ordinarily the round that should GOVERN this approval -- record THAT one with review-record'. In a pqnd-shaped backlog the globally-highest artifact is ALREADY recorded, so that assertion is false and following it re-creates the exact wedge R13-F1 reported. MEASURED, controlled fixture, real bd store, shipped scripts at HEAD adaf64d + uncommitted change set e86a9d59 (scratchpad/remedy-probe.sh). SHAPE B (r5-r9 recorded via review-record, r1-r4 planted unrecorded): 'review-check.sh gate' BEFORE any remedy = ok:true, artifact.iteration=9 (a WORKING selector). approve = exit 4, review_artifact_unrecorded; its advice names ...-r4.json (iteration=4). Following it verbatim -- review-record r4, then review-reconcile r1,r2,r3 -- yields 'gate' = ok:false, error_key=review_artifact_selection_disagreement, offending record pair reported by the gate itself as 'iteration=9 ... at=2026-09-09T20:52:06Z ||| iteration=4 ... at=2026-09-09T20:52:12Z', and approve = exit 4. So the printed remedy converted ok:true into a wedge. SHAPE A (i8cx-shaped: r1 recorded, r2-r4 planted, global max unrecorded) following the same advice = gate ok:true iteration=4, approve exit 0 -- the advice is correct only for this shape. SHAPE B-prime (identical pqnd fixture, review-reconcile on ALL FOUR, arbitrary order) = gate ok:true iteration=9, approve exit 0. Section 8.3 tests exactly B-prime, which is the CORRECT procedure and NOT the one the message prints, so L1 is green while the shipped advice is wrong: review-separation.test.sh PASSED 154/154 in my own full-tier run. The wedge IS recoverable -- I followed the review_artifact_selection_disagreement remedy (re-record the highest-iteration artifact, r9) and gate returned to ok:true iteration=9 -- hence high, not critical. R13-F1 asked for precisely this control in these words: 'reconcile a pqnd-shaped backlog ... in the order the SHIPPED refusal prints, assert approve reaches 0'. That leg does not exist. The correct rule is already written down one screen away, in qa-gate.sh's own usage text at :2956-2959 ('Reconciling every historic round through this command instead means only the round that should actually govern the release verdict is ever recorded through review-record'), and in the new docs/HOOKS.md paragraph -- both of which then defer to this message as the authority on 'when to use which'.
findings.description: The failing boundary is exactly max(unrecorded iteration) < max(recorded iteration); equality is impossible because one iteration derives one path. The data needed is already in hand at the refusal site: the per-file loop at :4951-4980 computes each on-disk artifact's hash and its membership in the recorded set, so the else-branch of :4969 is already 'this file IS recorded' -- tracking its iteration there is two lines and needs no new call. (review_out from review-check.sh gate at :4677 also carries .artifact.iteration = max(recorded) by K3, but it is inside the bypass_review guard, so the in-loop derivation is the more robust source.) Then: when max(unrecorded) > max(recorded), print today's advice unchanged; otherwise print 'the round that governs (iteration=N) is already recorded -- reconcile ALL of the files listed above and review-record none of them'. Ship it with the control R13-F1 specified: drive the pqnd fixture through the advice the message ACTUALLY PRINTS (parse it out of the refusal envelope, do not re-derive it in the test), assert approve reaches 0, and mutate the new comparison away to prove the leg fails without it. Section 8.1 already builds the wedge and 8.3 already builds the cure, so the missing leg sits between two fixtures that exist.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/tests/review-separation.test.sh:8.3f (the assertion that stands in for the safety property) and .claude/scripts/tests/review-count.test.sh section 15 (where the offline leg would belong)
findings.evidence: The entire safety argument for this round is that a RECONCILED record can never be a K3 selection candidate. Nothing asserts that under adversarial input. 8.3f asserts 'the governing record is UNTOUCHED after reconciliation (still iteration=9)' on a fixture whose reconciled iterations are 1-4 -- strictly BELOW the governing 9 -- so it would pass even if RECONCILED records were fully selectable. 8.5's META strip proves only that RECOGNITION in recorded-hashes is load-bearing (removing it makes approve refuse again); it cannot catch the opposite regression, a reader or trigger LOOSENED into selecting reconciled records. 8.4f pins the WRITER's grammar by regex, so a writer-side change is caught; the reader side and cmd_gate's trigger are not. Section 15 (429 assertions, the offline --comments-json seam where this is cheapest to test) contains no RECONCILED case at all. I verified the property myself instead, 15 cases via the --comments-json seam (scratchpad/adv-probe.sh): a reconciled record at iteration=999 against a governing iteration=3 leaves gate byte-identical to the no-reconciled-record BASELINE (rounds=1, rounds_basis=hash_equality, open_findings=1, independent=true, artifact.iteration=3, artifact_hash=1111...), and 11 crafted reason payloads -- an inline well-formed governing record, a newline followed by one, a newline followed by an INDENTED one (aimed at the rounds counter's looser ^[[:space:]]* anchor), a second ' at <ts>: ' marker aimed at extending reconciled_prefix_len, a second artifact_hash=, a newline plus RESOLVED R3-F1, a newline plus ARBITRATION overrule, a newline plus IMPLEMENTER, and a newline plus a second RECONCILED record with a different hash -- every one produced that same identical envelope. recorded-hashes reported count=2 in all 11 (never 3 for the injected second reconciled record) against count=1 at baseline. Reconciled-only (no governing record) = gate exit 4, review_artifact_missing, rounds=0, all artifact fields empty. Malformed reconciled (iteration=1.5) and INDENTED reconciled both = count 0, i.e. fail-closed; prose mention not at line start = count 0.
findings.description: The property HOLDS -- I established it by construction (all four readers of the comment stream reduce each comment to split("\n")[0] and anchor at ^: review-check.sh cmd_gate:2030+2601, its rounds counter:2996, cmd_recorded_hashes:1843+1875/1932, and qa-gate.sh finding_id_in_latest_artifact:6860-6862; and reconciled_prefix_len is deterministic because [0-9]+ and [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ both stop at the space that must precede the literal ' at ', so the reason is always outside substr($0,1,plen)) and then by measurement. This is therefore a missing regression guard, not a live defect. But it is the guard for the one claim the whole round rests on, and CLAUDE.md's pairing requirement is explicit that a new check ships with a negative control. Cheapest form, two legs: (a) in review-count.test.sh section 15, a RECONCILED record at iteration=999 alongside a governing iteration=3, asserting recorded-hashes returns BOTH hashes while gate's artifact.iteration stays 3; (b) the same fixture with a crafted reason carrying an embedded newline and a complete fake governing record, asserting gate's envelope is byte-identical to the reason-free case. Both run offline against --comments-json in milliseconds.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:7253-7263 (cmd_review_reconcile's stated non-goal) and :5003 (the refusal advice that points operators at it)
findings.evidence: review-reconcile validates the artifact via validate-artifact and therefore already has .verdict and .findings[].severity in hand, but never looks at them. MEASURED (scratchpad/guard-probe.sh, case G7): a task with a clean governing r1 recorded, plus an unrecorded r5 on disk carrying verdict=findings and one CRITICAL finding. Before: gate open_findings=0, artifact.iteration=1; approve exit 4 review_artifact_unrecorded (correct -- the new refusal caught it). After 'review-reconcile r5': gate open_findings=0, artifact.iteration=1 STILL, and approve exit 0, status=approved. The critical finding never entered the trust chain, and the reviewer who raised it is recorded only as a hash in a non-governing pointer record.
findings.description: This is NOT a regression: with the k6re block absent, that same approve also succeeded and left no record at all, so review-reconcile restores the pre-fix outcome while adding an audited, hash-bound record and a mandatory operator reason. The header at :7253-7263 states the non-goal explicitly and says 'This command does not attempt to detect that case; the operator names it via the required reason argument instead.' What makes it worth recording anyway is that the refusal message at :5003 now actively instructs operators to run review-reconcile on 'every OTHER listed file' with no severity qualifier, so the sharp edge sits directly downstream of a printed instruction rather than only in expert hands -- and it composes with R14-F1, where an operator working a pqnd-shaped backlog is told to reconcile several files at once. A mechanical guard is cheap and needs no new data: refuse (or at minimum warn in the envelope) when the artifact being reconciled has verdict=findings AND at least one findings[].severity that ranks at or above its own risk_threshold, with the existing bypass-reason discipline as the escape. I am NOT asking for a third reader of the record stream (qa.md forbids that, jio.1) -- everything needed is inside the JSON review-reconcile already parses.

findings.evidence: The comment justifying --accept-unrecorded-review states 'i8cx and pqnd are both CLOSED today, so this refusal cannot strand either of them right now'. MEASURED at HEAD adaf64d: 'bd show claude-workflow-plugin-i8cx --json | jq .status' returns in_progress, with labels backend,devops,qa-approved. pqnd, xsu1 and 6im2 are genuinely closed. So half the claim is false, and the live exposure it denies is real: i8cx carries 9 unrecorded artifacts (12 on disk, recorded-hashes count=3, per-file sha256 membership check), so a fresh approve on it refuses today.
findings.description: No behavioural consequence -- the bypass exists either way, and i8cx happens to be i8cx-SHAPED (its global max r12 is itself unrecorded, so R14-F1's advice would work there), so this is exposure rather than harm. Recorded because the sentence is the stated justification for keeping a bypass: a future maintainer who reads 'both CLOSED, cannot strand either' and later confirms both closed has been handed an argument for removing an escape that is still load-bearing. Fix is one clause -- name the measured statuses, or drop the status claim and keep the surrounding reasoning, which stands on its own ('a task reopened for a fresh approval with old unrecorded artifacts still on disk needs an escape').

findings.location: CHANGELOG.md ([Unreleased]/### Added, the qa-gate.sh approve bullet) and docs/HOOKS.md:2614 (the qa-gate.sh table row)
findings.evidence: Both say the refusal names the file(s) 'and the SHA-256 of each' / 'naming the file(s) and their SHA-256'. Three of the four per-file sub-cases in the loop at qa-gate.sh:4951-4980 cannot produce a hash and name a reason instead: 'outside docs/reviews/ -- a symlink out of the declared directory' (:4954), 'not a regular file -- a directory or other non-file object at this path' (:4961, which is the R13-F6 fix from my own previous round), and 'unhashable, rc=N' (:4966). MEASURED (scratchpad/f1-dep-probe.sh case 3): a task with a DIRECTORY at ...-r2.json and a real artifact at ...-r3.json refuses with both listed, the first as 'not a regular file -- ... cannot corroborate' and only the second as 'sha256=9b0050b1...'.
findings.description: Everything else I checked in the two files is accurate, and I verified the two load-bearing claims independently rather than reading them: (1) docs/HOOKS.md's 'a second, independent review-related refusal ... --no-review does NOT waive it' -- reproduced, approve with --no-review --no-completion --no-design still exits 4 with review_artifact_unrecorded; (2) verify-before-stop.sh's new comment claim that 'a k6re-stripped build releases (rc=0) where the shipped build blocks (rc=4) on an identical missing review-check.sh' -- reproduced exactly, shipped build exit 4 review_check_unavailable, UNRECORDED-REVIEW-ARTIFACT-REFUSAL-stripped build exit 0 approved, with the F1 arm's own invocation at verify-before-stop.sh:4539-4544 confirmed to pass --no-review and no --accept-unrecorded-review slot. Also verified: the refusal's placement claim ('between REVIEW-SEPARATION and the completion-contract check' -- REVIEW-SEPARATION END is :4831, this block :4833-5010, the P7 completion fields :5012); 'up to 12 artifacts on disk against 3 recorded rounds' (i8cx, exact); 'pqnd, 9 against 5' (exact); the recorded-hashes UNION-not-K3 description; and the whole two-shape backfill account. Fix is a word: 'and, where one can be computed, the SHA-256 of each'.

findings.evidence: The R13-F3 fix added review_artifact_unrecorded and review_check_unavailable to the enumeration. The new block emits a THIRD exit-4 error_key that is not named: review_recorded_hashes_unavailable (qa-gate.sh:4933), fired when review-check.sh is present but recorded-hashes fails -- e.g. .beads absent, which review-check.sh:1825-1827 answers with bd_unavailable/exit 2. Counted at HEAD: 'grep -c review_recorded_hashes_unavailable' returns 1 in qa-gate.sh, 0 in verify-before-stop.sh, 0 in docs/HOOKS.md, 0 in CHANGELOG.md. It is reachable from the F1 arm for the same degraded-install reason as review_check_unavailable, which the enumeration does name.
findings.description: Same class as the finding it partially closes: the enumeration's whole purpose is that 'the availability cost is stated rather than discovered', and one of three new keys is still discoverable-only. One bullet, next to the review_check_unavailable bullet it shares a failure mode with.

findings.evidence: The comment says the free-text reason is 'matching every other writer in this file (review-record own summary, resolve-finding own summary, arbitrate own rationale)'. review-record does not belong in that list: its summary is machine-generated at :7202-7206, either 'approve — no findings at/above <rt>' or 'findings — <n> finding(s) reported', with no operator-supplied text anywhere in the record. resolve-finding and arbitrate do take operator free text, so the family claim holds for two of the three.
findings.description: Cosmetic, and the safety argument the sentence makes is sound on its own terms -- anchored parsers never read past the marker they require, which is why the 11 reason-injection payloads in R14-F2 all failed. Recorded only because review-record is the writer a reader would most likely check first, and finding no operator free text there could be read as the comment describing a guard that is not present. Drop 'review-record own summary' from the list.

findings.location: .claude/scripts/qa-gate.sh:3354-3362 (add_comment) as consumed by cmd_review_reconcile:7441-7442 and cmd_review_record:7209-7210
findings.evidence: add_comment swallows a failed bd write into log_sync_error and always returns success, so both recorders emit ok:true / status=recorded / 'comment posted at <ts>' even when no comment was written. Observed accidentally and then confirmed: my first probe run invoked qa-gate.sh with cwd at the repo root while the fixture task lived in a fixture store, so every bd comments add failed; review-record still returned {"ok":true,...,"status":"recorded"} with a full record in observations, and review-check.sh gate on the same task reported review_artifact_missing. I re-checked the repo store afterwards for contamination -- 0 probe tasks present, bd count 489, and bd show of a fixture id from the repo cwd errors -- so nothing leaked.
findings.description: Pre-existing and inherited, not introduced this round: the add_comment comment explains itself as 'Comments are non-authoritative (labels are the source of truth)', which is true for the QA-GATE audit comments it was written for and false for these two subcommands, where the comment IS the record and the file on disk is worthless without it. review-reconcile inherits it verbatim. Not proposing a fix inside this task's scope -- it touches every writer in the file, and the honest change (have the record writers check the write) is a separate piece of work. Recorded so the next pass does not read status=recorded as evidence a record exists; the only trustworthy confirmation is review-check.sh recorded-hashes or gate.
